text:
maria (eng-runtime): Heads-up: we've been seeing higher tail latency on gpu-rack-11 since ~01:45 UTC. Preliminary metrics point to PCIe AER floods and NVLink resets.
raj (eng-infra): Copy. Which hosts are noisy?
maria (eng-runtime): gpu-node-21 and gpu-node-22. nvlink_link_flap_count spiked ~01:46 and pci_bus_reset_total incremented several times. Also Xid 79/31 messages in dmesg.
sasha (eng-sre): Can you paste the relevant snippets from journal + nvidia error stats?
maria (eng-runtime): Logs attached below:
```
-- journalctl --since "2025-12-02 01:40:00" -u kubelet -n 60 --no-pager
Dec 02 01:45:58 gpu-node-21 kernel: NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:3c:00.0): 31, pid=0, Channel exception
Dec 02 01:46:02 gpu-node-21 kernel: pcieport 0000:6a:00.0: AER: Multiple Uncorrected (Non-Fatal) Error messages
Dec 02 01:46:05 gpu-node-21 kernel: nvlink0: link 0 down
Dec 02 01:46:07 gpu-node-21 kernel: nvlink0: link 0 up
Dec 02 01:48:12 gpu-node-22 kernel: pcieport 0000:6a:00.0: AER: Corrected error received: ID 0040
```
```
# nvidia-smi -q -d ERRORS -i 0
GPU 0:
    Xid Errors: 4
    PCI Bus Resets: 3
    NVLink Link Flaps: 7
```

ashley (eng-runtime): Are both GPUs under the same PCIe switch or is that coincidence?
raj (eng-infra): lspci shows both behind bridge 0000:6a:00.0. Likely shared switch (or motherboard trace). Could be firmware issue or bad riser.
nvmon-bot: Alert: nvlink_link_flap_count > 5 on cluster/gpu-rack-11 (severity: WARNING)

sasha (eng-sre): Immediate triage plan: 1) cordon + drain affected nodes, 2) ensure batch jobs are preempted first, 3) capture full lspci -vvv and setpci registers, 4) run minimal repro to try to trigger AER in lab image.
maria (eng-runtime): Starting cordon + drain for gpu-node-21. Will redirect batch jobs away first.
raj (eng-infra): Before any reboots, capture: `lspci -vvv -s 6a:00.0`, `setpci -s 6a:00.0 CAP_EXP+0x04.L` (AER status), and `dmidecode` for motherboard revision.
nashley (eng-runtime): Let's also freeze autoscaler for 15m to avoid shocking the cluster.

maria (eng-runtime): Copied outputs:
```
lspci -vvv -s 6a:00.0
# Bridge: Vendor ABC, Device PCIe Switch, AER: enabled, Uncorr error mask: 0x0, Uncorr error severity: NonFatal
```

raj (eng-infra): I pulled kernel AER counters: corrected_count rising, but also bursts of uncorrected non-fatal errors. That aligns with repeated NVLink resets.
sasha (eng-sre): Alert tuning: change nvlink flaps > 4 in 10m -> Pager, pci_bus_reset delta > 1 in 15m -> Pager. Current rules are too lax.

vendor-support-bot: Opened ticket #VND-4780 with OEM. Attached kernel logs and nvidia-smi dumps. Engineer will triage in ~3-5 hours.

ashley (eng-runtime): For mitigation: prefer rescheduling latency-tolerant batch jobs off the rack and keep realtime endpoints on other racks. Label workloads with `gpu_tier: realtime` and `gpu_tier: batch` and evict batch first.
maria (eng-runtime): Doing that now: evicted batch pods on gpu-rack-11. Cordon completed for gpu-node-21 at 1752003505.

raj (eng-infra): I have a spare NVLink bridge and spare riser in lab. If vendor doesn't provide immediate remediation, we can swap riser/bridge during a short maintenance window and test. Will log hardware inventory and pre-stage parts.

ashley (eng-runtime): Can we reproduce? I'll run a focused allreduce stress using NCCL on a test node to try and force NVLink traffic. Script: `python stress_allreduce.py --iters 50 --msg-size 64MB`
sasha (eng-sre): Good. Also add a temporary circuit-breaker in our traffic router to cap collective op concurrency from the app-layer to prevent cascading resets.

maria (eng-runtime): After draining node-21, node-22 still shows sporadic AER messages when under load. Keeping it cordoned and out of rotation.

raj (eng-infra): Physical check scheduled for today afternoon. If we observe identical AER events on both nodes tied to same PCIe bridge, leaning toward switch firmware or motherboard trace fault. RMA plan in motion if vendor confirms.

vendor-support-bot: Vendor update on #VND-4780: "Initial analysis suggests PCIe switch firmware race condition causing AER storms under parallel NVLink traffic. Requesting repro steps and logs."

ashley (eng-runtime): Short-term: throttle per-GPU concurrency to 1 on affected nodes via device plugin config, and update runtime to prefer healthy nodes for low-latency routes.
sasha (eng-sre): Action list:
- raj: collect lspci, setpci, hw topology, open RMA if vendor confirms; escalate in 3h if no engineer assigned
- maria: finish draining remaining targets, evict batch first, monitor SLOs & costs
- ashley: provide repro script + run in lab, add router circuit-breaker rules
- sasha: bump alert severities and prepare postmortem template

maria (eng-runtime): Note on cost: draining gpu-rack-11 will push ~100 jobs to other racks and may trigger extra on-demand provisioning in us-west-2; estimate +25% infra spend this hour if we keep capacity for low-latency jobs.

raj (eng-infra): Noted. Will try swaps in lab first. Marking gpu-node-22 as DO NOT SCHEDULE until replaced or validated.

vendor-support-bot: Vendor engineer assigned and requested concrete repro. Ticket #VND-4780 updated.

maria (eng-runtime): Will post updates after hardware swap attempt or vendor root-cause. Thanks all. :white_check_mark:
